name: Air Fryer Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce and Rice

components.name: Satay Chicken

ingredients.name: Raw boneless chicken breast, long strips

steps: Combine chicken strips with measured oil, soy, ginger, garlic, turmeric, chili flakes and lime. Cover and marinate refrigerated for at least one hour.
Air fry chicken at approximately 195 C in spaced batches for 12-16 minutes, turning, until it reaches 74 C internally.
Portion cooked chicken, rice and broccoli into four containers. Keep peanut sauce separate for drizzling after reheating; thin with water if needed.
Cool promptly and freeze meal components if required, but sauce may separate after thawing and should be stirred vigorously.

components.name: Jasmine Rice & Broccoli
steps: Cook jasmine rice with its measured water; lightly steam broccoli.

components.name: Peanut Sauce
steps: Mix peanut butter, coconut cream, soy, lime, maple syrup and curry powder with enough measured water to achieve a pourable sauce; keep separate from the raw chicken.

Planning: Secondary stovetop for rice and vegetables; marinate at least 1 hour.
Freezer: chicken and rice freeze; coconut peanut sauce may separate
Dietary: Peanuts, soy, coconut; wheat in regular soy sauce.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; freeze later-week portions soon after cooking.
Reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. Cook poultry and ground turkey to 74 C. For whole pork cuts, cook to at least 63 C with a 3-minute rest.
When a recipe includes rice, cool it rapidly and store cold immediately; avoid leaving cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Reheat crisp foods in oven or air fryer when possible.
